title: Winking Face with Tongue Emoji 😜 Meaning: Just Kidding
description: The winking face with tongue emoji 😜 means the sender is joking, teasing or flirting and wants you to know it. See how the wink changes a message.
summary: 😜 is a wink with the tongue stuck out, and it marks a message as a joke, a tease or a bit of flirting. The wink says “you know what I mean” and the tongue says “don't take this seriously.” It usually appears right after a cheeky line to soften it.
meaning: Most of the time 😜 works as a tone tag. Someone writes something that could sting or sound forward if read flat, then adds this face so the other person hears it as banter. “Guess I'm the favorite child now 😜” is a boast nobody is meant to believe. The emoji carries the same job that “jk” or “lol” does, but with more mischief and a suggestion that the sender is rather pleased with themselves.

The wink is what separates it from the other tongue-out faces. A wink implies a shared secret, so 😜 leans toward inside jokes and flirting in a way that plain 😛 does not. Sent to a friend, it reads as goofing around. Sent to someone you have been trading compliments with, it reads as intentional, especially after a line that could be taken two ways. That double reading is exactly why people like it: the message stays deniable.

It also has a party-mode life. Captions about a night out, a spontaneous trip or a decision that was probably unwise often end with 😜, where it means something like “no regrets.” This use was everywhere in the early 2010s, and the emoji still carries a little of that era. Many younger users now reach for 🤪, 😭 or 💀 to show they are joking, so a message full of 😜 can come across as earnest and slightly dated rather than edgy.

None of that makes it wrong to use. It remains one of the clearest ways to say “I am teasing you, please don't be offended,” and it is understood across age groups. The main risk is the opposite of confusion: it is so obviously playful that it can feel like you are explaining your own joke.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Between friends, 😜 follows a dig, a brag or a dare. It tells the reader the sarcasm is friendly. It often closes the message rather than standing alone, because its purpose is to change how the words before it are heard. As a solo reply it usually means “wouldn't you like to know” or “hehe, caught me.”

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: After a compliment or a suggestive remark, 😜 is light flirting with an escape hatch. The sender can always claim they were only joking. One 😜 after a joke about your terrible music taste is not a declaration, but a pattern of teasing messages that keep ending this way usually signals interest and an invitation to tease back.

contexts.label: In captions
contexts.body: On Instagram and Facebook it tags selfies with a tongue out, vacation chaos, and photos where the poster is being deliberately silly. It often sits next to party and drink emojis. Brands use it for jokey promotions, which is part of why some people now associate it with marketing copy and group chats run by older relatives.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: It is fine in a casual team channel after an obvious joke, such as volunteering a coworker for the next presentation. Avoid it in anything directed at clients or senior people you do not know well. The wink can read as overfamiliar, and a tongue-out face undercuts a message that needs to be taken at face value.

examples.text: I let you win that last round 😜
examples.meaning: A friendly taunt after losing a game; the sender does not expect to be believed.

examples.text: Somebody looked very good in that story today 😜
examples.meaning: A flirty compliment delivered as a tease, so it feels low pressure.

examples.text: Booked the flights before checking my bank account 😜
examples.meaning: Owning an impulsive decision and treating it as a fun story instead of a problem.

examples.text: Don't worry, I only told like five people 😜
examples.meaning: Joking about spilling a secret; the wink signals the sender actually kept quiet.

examples.text: You're buying dinner then, since you're so rich now 😜
examples.meaning: Teasing a friend about a raise or a win without any real expectation.

examples.text: What happens at the bachelorette stays at the bachelorette 😜
examples.meaning: Hinting at wild stories while playfully refusing to share details.

combos.meaning: A night out is planned or underway, and it is expected to get a little rowdy.
The sender is cracking up at their own joke and making sure you know it was a joke.
Flirting that mixes teasing with real affection, common between partners.
A secret is being kept, and the sender is enjoying having it.

confusedWith.difference: 😛 has both eyes open and no wink, so it is simple silliness or a childish “nyah nyah.” 😜 adds the wink, which brings in innuendo, inside jokes and flirting that the plain version lacks.

🤪 has mismatched eyes and a tilted head, and it means the sender feels chaotic or unhinged. 😜 is more controlled: a deliberate tease aimed at the reader, not a description of the sender's own mental state.

😉 is a smoother wink used for hints, flirting and gentle irony. 😜 is the goofier cousin. Adding the tongue lowers the smoothness and raises the silliness, making it harder to read as a serious come-on.

avoid: Skip it after real criticism, because a tongue-out wink does not turn an insult into a joke.
Do not use it to flirt with someone who has not flirted back, since the wink can feel presumptuous.
Leave it out of apologies and bad news, where it makes you look like you are not taking the situation seriously.
design: A yellow face with one eye open wide, the other closed in a wink, and a tongue sticking out of a grinning mouth. Which eye winks and how far the tongue extends differ slightly from vendor to vendor, and several older designs looked wilder than the current ones. The modern Apple, Google, Samsung and Microsoft versions are all easy to recognize as the same expression.

faqs.a: It can be. The wink suggests a shared secret, so after a compliment or a suggestive line it reads as flirting. After an ordinary joke between friends it is just teasing. Look at the sentence it follows and at whether the person teases you this way often.

faqs.q: What does 😜 mean from a guy or a girl?
faqs.a: There is no gendered meaning. From anyone, it marks the message as playful. If it follows a comment about how you look or about spending time together, treat it as mild flirting; if it follows a joke at your expense, they are checking that you are still on friendly terms.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 😜 and 😝?
faqs.a: 😜 winks, so it is directed at you and often carries a hint or a tease. 😝 has both eyes squeezed shut and is more of a self-contained reaction: blowing a raspberry, gloating, or reacting to something gross or over the top.

It is less common among teens and people in their twenties than it was in the 2010s, and some see it as a millennial or parent emoji. It is still widely used and fully understood, so the only cost is sounding a bit more earnest than ironic.

faqs.q: When did the 😜 emoji come out?
faqs.a: It was part of the first big wave of emojis standardized in Unicode in 2010, carried over from Japanese mobile phone sets, and it has been on iPhone and Android keyboards for as long as those keyboards have existed in their modern form.
